justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Catalogue Service and Search Engine provide browsing, Shopping Cart & Checkout Service manages orders, Review Service handles ratings, and DynamoDB Streams integrates with Recommendation Engine. Localization & Currency Service and Shipping Provider APIs satisfy multi-currency and logistics constraints.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The design uses Amazon CloudFront for SPA asset delivery, Amazon ElastiCache for fast currency lookups, and Amazon DynamoDB for low-latency catalogue reads. Asynchronous offloading via Amazon SQS and EventBridge ensures high throughput to easily handle 1M MAU and meet page load targets.
justifications.compatibility: The architecture integrates cleanly with external systems via defined interfaces: Payment Gateway via tokenized HTTPS, Shipping Provider APIs via mTLS, Recommendation Engine (AWS Personalize) via DynamoDB Streams, and Third-Party Financial APIs via Exchange Rate Sync Worker.
justifications.usability: Shopper/Reviewer journeys are supported by dedicated React components (Catalogue & Search View, Cart & Checkout Flow, Review & Rating Widget). However, Store Administrator interactions rely solely on the generic SPA shell without specialized administrative components or views detailed.
justifications.reliability: The 99.95% uptime target is supported through multi-AZ Aurora Distributed Storage (6-way replication), DynamoDB Global Tables across the three target regions, ElastiCache Global Datastores, SQS asynchronous buffering, and circuit breakers in the Currency Conversion Component.
justifications.security: Security is addressed with AWS WAF for OWASP Top-10 defenses, Lambda Authorizer for JWT/RBAC, mTLS between internal gRPC services, and AWS Secrets Manager. Explicit mechanisms for CCPA/GDPR compliance are referenced, though detailed audit logging mechanisms are omitted.
justifications.maintainability: High maintainability is achieved through microservice modularity (Catalogue, Review, Cart/Checkout, Localization), separation of concerns in SPA components, loose coupling via Amazon EventBridge, and well-defined component responsibilities like Currency & Tax Adapter and Moderation & Sanitization Engine.
justifications.portability: The system achieves multi-region adaptability across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1. However, replaceability is low due to tight coupling with proprietary AWS services, including Aurora Serverless v2, DynamoDB Global Tables, EventBridge, API Gateway, and AWS Personalize.

PERF-01.justification: CloudFront CDN, S3, DynamoDB, and ElastiCache absorb read spikes effectively. ECS Fargate autoscales stateless backend services. However, lacking a dedicated search cluster like OpenSearch may strain Redis and DynamoDB under 10x complex keyword querying.
sensitivity_points: CloudFront cache hit ratios on catalogue pages
tradeoffs: Aggressive read caching reduces latency but introduces temporary catalogue data staleness

PERF-02.justification: Recommendation workloads are fully offloaded to external AWS Personalize via asynchronous DynamoDB Streams. Background CDC processing completely isolates recommendation recomputations from synchronous catalogue browsing and read paths.
sensitivity_points: Asynchronous stream processing rate from DynamoDB Streams
Decoupled execution boundaries between recommendation ML and read models
tradeoffs: Asynchronous batch recommendation decoupling risks serving slightly outdated personalized suggestions

AVAIL-01.justification: Checkout Orchestrator decouples transactional checkout by persisting orders to Aurora and queuing fulfillment asynchronously to Amazon SQS. However, real-time shipping rate lookup failures during checkout are not explicitly mitigated with fallback rate strategies.
sensitivity_points: SQS queue durability and asynchronous fulfillment worker retry policies
Fallback pricing mechanisms when shipping estimation endpoints fail
tradeoffs: Asynchronous fulfillment prevents order dropouts but may cause shipping cost discrepancies

AVAIL-02.justification: While DynamoDB Global Tables and ElastiCache Global Datastore span multi-region deployments, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is architected solely with multi-AZ replication within a single region. If us-east-1 experiences an outage, transactional checkout data cannot fail over.
sensitivity_points: Cross-region replication mechanisms for transactional relational databases
RPO and RTO thresholds during regional cloud failure
tradeoffs: Multi-region database replication maintains cross-region availability at the cost of write latency

MOD-01.justification: The dedicated Localization & Currency Service encapsulates exchange rate lookups, sync workers, and caching. Adding JPY requires updating rates via financial APIs and currency adapter configuration, leaving catalogue and core services unaffected.
sensitivity_points: Extensible currency enumeration in conversion configuration
Isolation of currency conversion logic behind internal gRPC boundaries
tradeoffs: Centralized currency service enhances modularity but introduces network hops during checkout

MOD-02.justification: The recommendation system is fully encapsulated as an external engine fed via DynamoDB Streams change data capture. Swapping or tuning the algorithm requires no architectural or code modifications across the bookstore services.
sensitivity_points: Standardized event schema delivered via DynamoDB Streams
Clean separation between ML recommendation generation and catalogue APIs
tradeoffs: Decoupled ML interfaces reduce deployment dependencies but restrict custom real-time transactional features

SEC-01.justification: AWS WAF filters malicious payloads at ingress. Search uses DynamoDB key lookups, and Review Service implements a Moderation & Sanitization Engine alongside TypeORM parameterized queries, comprehensively mitigating OWASP Top-10 SQLi and XSS risks.
sensitivity_points: Comprehensive WAF rule sets covering OWASP Top-10 signatures
Strict query parameterization within ORM data access layers
tradeoffs: Deep payload inspection and sanitization increase ingress processing latency slightly

SEC-02.justification: User identity and profile management services are entirely missing from the architecture. While localization has zero-persistence, personal data persisted across Aurora (orders, reviews) and DynamoDB (carts) lacks any automated deletion orchestration or auditing pipeline.
sensitivity_points: Absence of a centralized identity service managing user records
Coordinated deletion orchestration across polyglot persistent datastores
tradeoffs: Decentralized data storage isolates bounded contexts but drastically complicates unified CCPA/GDPR erasure
